archetypes.name: cross-doc-sync
archetypes.rationale: The plan edits two normative routing files (SKILL.md + approval-gates.md) in parallel; semantic drift between them is the primary defect risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the Step 3.6 disposition matrix described in SKILL.md against the routing clauses in approval-gates.md, checking that every status listed in one file has an equivalent and non-contradictory clause in the other. Look for statuses that appear in SKILL.md short-circuit lists but are absent or differently categorized in approval-gates.md Gate B/C tables, and vice versa. Pay particular attention to main-agent-vote-required, panel-failed, and cap-reached, which appear in both files but with subtly different prose. Check whether the passive-summary Continue branch is described identically in both files with respect to Step 3.6 ordering relative to Gate C and the next Step 3 entry. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: status-matrix
archetypes.rationale: The plan must assign an explicit Step 3.6 disposition to every known Step 3 exit status; any omitted status is a silent fail-open gap.
archetypes.prompt_body: Enumerate every distinct LOOP_STATUS and TALLY_PLAN_REVIEW_STATUS value referenced anywhere in skills/design/SKILL.md and skills/design/references/approval-gates.md, then verify the plan assigns an explicit Step 3.6 disposition—either route-through or a named skip breadcrumb—to each one without gaps. Look especially for statuses mentioned only in passing in the plan text but absent from explicit skip or route lists. Check whether zero-findings-degraded-panel is correctly kept out of skip lists per plan intent, and whether the main-agent-vote-required handling covers both the success re-tally path and the tally-error fallback without leaving an unresolved disposition. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: fixture-isolation
archetypes.rationale: The integration test has complex mock-export and case-local isolation requirements; incorrect sequencing causes mock leakage between cases that would invalidate the behavioral guard.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine the plan's integration test design for test-assess-plan-round.sh, focusing on whether the case-local mock export sequence, artifact reset scope, and run-params.json placement are self-consistent with the existing harness structure. Check that Entry 1 and Entry 2 share the same case_tmp without an inter-entry reset, that case-local dispatch and monitor stubs are exported immediately before Entry 1 and cannot be overwritten by earlier test cases, and that LARCH_TALLY_PLAN_ASSESSOR_SH points to the real tally script rather than a stub. Verify that the plan's assertion list (ASSESSOR_STATUS, ASSESSOR_VERDICT, EFFECTIVE_ASSESSORS, file existence checks for both round snapshots) is sufficient to detect the fail-open false positive scenario described in the plan's Failure Modes section without relying on inherited global state. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
